world.bio: Dale Whitcombe, 43, Victoria BC. Spent fifteen years in forestry, cruising timber and planting, then switched nine years ago to guiding foraging walks on southern Vancouver Island. Chanterelles in fall, morels in spring, lobster mushrooms and hedgehogs in between. Keeps getting inquiries in Mandarin about chanterelle and matsutake walks and wants to launch Mandarin-language tours in spring 2027. Small groups, six at a time, with a hot lunch in the field.
skills_assets: Nine years of foraging walks, around 1,100 clients served
Provincial and regional park permits for commercial guiding in four areas near Sooke and Port Renfrew
Knows 40+ edible species cold, a working field ID set and a pressed-spore print collection
Keeps a client email list of about 2,300 and a website with a booking calendar
A 2017 Ford Transit with seats for eight and a trailer for gear
First Aid Level 3 and a wilderness first responder ticket

projects.name: Fall 2026 foraging season
projects.text: Peak chanterelle season runs through mid-October. 34 walks booked so far. Forty percent of them are tourists from Asia coming off cruise ships at Victoria, and half of those ask about matsutake even though we only get a few. Booked solid on weekends.

projects.name: Mandarin-language tour idea
projects.text: Over the past two years I have had maybe 120 emails in Mandarin, plus WeChat messages from a couple of tour operators in Vancouver asking whether I do group walks in Chinese. I answer with Google Translate and then feel bad. The idea is to launch Mandarin-language tours in spring 2027, probably April for early morels, and fold chanterelles into the fall. Haven't worked out who would guide, how to cover tasting if people eat what we find, or whether my insurance would let me.

projects.name: Cabin deck rebuild
projects.text: Ripped out the rotted deck on the cabin in Sooke. Pressure-treated joists in, cedar decking going on in October if the rain holds. Eating into the foraging income.

notes.text: First big chanterelle flush of the season on the Sooke Hills side. 11 kg in two hours. Rain on Sunday did it. Didn't bring enough bags.

Another email in Mandarin today. Subject line was 'Do you have a guide who speaks Chinese for matsutake?' I translated it. They wanted three days of walks in October. I said I couldn't, we are English only. Replied with a polite no. Third time this month.
Mia's swim meet in Nanaimo. Seven hours round trip, ferry delays, three 100m fly heats. She dropped two seconds. Proud dad, tired dad. Her coach thinks she might make provincials.

Cider day. Neighbour Howard's apples, 140 kg. Pressed with the old hand press. Added crabapples this time for tannin. 60 litres in the carboy. Smells like it'll be good. Last year's batch went flat by March.

Guided a group today: two couples from Taipei. Their English was fine, but they kept whispering to each other in Chinese, then looked at me, then at the mushrooms. I think they were asking whether to eat. I told them not to eat anything I hadn't confirmed. Wish I had spoken enough Mandarin to say the real details. Could have taught them so much more.

Looked into the insurance for tasting. Broker said any tour where clients eat wild mushrooms needs a documented ID protocol, preferably from a mycologist. Haven't done that. My own ID is solid but it's a one-man opinion. Put it on the list.
Deck: rain delay again. Joists are sitting under a tarp. Daughter says 'Dad, you said August.' Yes, I said August.
Bought a used Thermos for field soup. Lentil and chorizo, three litres. The Port Renfrew group loved it last week. Also lost a good knife somewhere near Jordan River. Annoyed.

Counted up. 34 walks, 214 clients, roughly 31,000 CAD for the season so far. Good year, and the Mandarin demand is the bit I keep tripping on. Everyone says 'next year'. It is next year in six months.

messages.text:
Karen: Don't forget Mia's thing is at 7.
Me: I'll pick her up from school.
Karen: And buy milk.
Me: Milk, noted.

Operator: We have a group of 12 retired teachers from Shanghai, want to do a foraging walk. Mandarin guide?
Me: Sorry, English only for now. Possibly next spring.
Operator: OK, keep in touch.

Howard: How did the cider come out?
Me: Still bubbling.
Howard: You owe me a bottle.
Me: You owe me a hand with the deck.

Broker: For tasting events we'd want a written protocol.
Me: What kind of protocol?
Broker: Species list, ID method, who signs off.
Me: I'll look into it.

Ranger: Permits for next season are open Nov 1.
Me: Thanks, will apply.
Ranger: Remember to log your harvest numbers.

constraints: Groups capped at 8; permits allow no more
Won't guide in the heat of August
Can't run walks every weekend; family time Sundays in winter
Won't offer tasting without proper insurance cover
sensitive: Insurance coverage unclear for tasting; fear of a poisoning claim
Income is seasonal; January to March is thin
